newsitem.title: ESTONIA: MARKET GENERALLY WELCOMES RAKVERE ACTION.
newsitem.headline: MARKET GENERALLY WELCOMES RAKVERE ACTION.

text.p: Dealers and analysts were pleased on Wednesday with the decisiveness of regulators in suspending Rakvere shares amid insider trading allegations but felt the bourse gave too little information.

Rakvere was earlier suspended as the securities commission has asked the police to investigate whether insider dealing was involved when its shares rose sharply just before it announced the purchase of Latvia's Rigas Miesnieks.
"It set a very good precedent," said Katrin Kaarli, Hansapank analyst, about the suspension.
"It shows the laws and regulations, which investors depend on, are in place and will be used if necessary," she added.
Traders also saw it as good move.
"It was a wise thing to do and it set a very good example," said Mattias Mustonen, trader at Hoiupank.
Some dealers were cautious, saying that they still do not have enough information from the bourse on what has happening.
"The bad thing about this is that the bourse release was too short, we still need more information," another trader said.
Rakvere shares, which were suspended at 14.05 kroons with two deals done, were expected to suffer from the news.
Talinna Pank trader Rein Ratsepp said he did not want to buy shares in a company that could be suspended at any time.
"Of course it will not be good for the company and its shares," one dealer said.
"The investigation could take months and what will happen to the stock during this time?" another analyst said.
